newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Elephants trample SAfrican soldier to death.
newsitem.headline: Elephants trample SAfrican soldier to death.

text.p: A soldier was trampled to death when a herd of some 70 elephants rampaged through a camp in a South African wildlife park, an official said on Friday.

Defence Force spokeswoman Lieutenant-Colonel Hester Boshoff said about 10 soldiers, patrolling the eastern border of the Kruger National Park for illegal immigrants from Mozambique, had set up a temporary tented camp in the bush.
"The herd of about 70 elephants -- which included numerous calves -- for some or other reason stormed the tents. The camp was protected only by a roll of barbed wire," Boshoff said.
She said the camp had not been established on the usual route of the herd.
"The soldiers panicked and fled in all directions. When they regrouped later, they discovered that Rifleman Len Nthene was missing...His body was discovered after an extended search," she said.
The incident took place on Friday last week, but was only reported this Friday.

In other incident, state radio reported that three people narrowly escaped death on Wednesday night when their car hit a hippo which had been living on the outskirts of Pretoria since it wandered out of a a nature reserve a few months ago.
The hippo cow died in the collision while one of the passengers, Elb Weideman, sustained a leg fracture and bruises.
